items.title: 'Happening in every university': Students sent to Putin's 'meat grinder'
items.description: Lessons look a little different at some universities and technical colleges around Russia this year, as the Kremlin tries to entice students to enlist in the military to cover massive casualties in Ukraine.

items.title: Famous outback race claims another life after serious motorbike crash
items.description: A motorbike rider has died in the Central Australian outback after a Finke Desert Race crash, with the two-day event expected to continue as police investigate.

items.title: Daniel Turpin named as diver killed in WA shark attack
items.description: The family of a 35-year-old diver who died after being bitten by a shark has described him as "an adored husband, son, brother and uncle who had a lifelong love and deep respect for the ocean".

items.title: As rape allegations engulf MAFS UK, Channel 4's former boss says the risks were always there
items.description: Married at First Sight UK could be axed as its broadcaster, Channel 4, awaits an external review into the program and serious rape allegations before "deciding what happens next".

items.title: Pauline Hanson tells Ben Roberts-Smith supporters she's 'walked in his shoes'
items.description: Pauline Hanson says, like Ben Roberts-Smith, she knows what it's like to face a criminal trial.

items.title: Who gets to write symphonies beyond Beethoven and why it matters
items.description: Beethoven's Ninth has topped the ABC Classic 100 countdown for the fifth time. We explore its mystique and shed light on composers following in Beethoven's footsteps.

items.title: Live: Swans win last-gasp thriller despite Ryan's mark of the year contender
items.description: Jai Serong kicks a last-minute goal to earn Sydney a two-point win over St Kilda, after the Swans had trailed by as many as 33 points in the first half. Follow live.

items.title: 'Embarrassing' Tigers humiliated by Penrith, Sharks down Dragons
items.description: The Penrith Panthers thrash Wests 68-0 to record the biggest win in club history, as Cronulla notches a 34-12 victory over St George Illawarra at Shark Park.

items.title: Inside a Trump-linked plan to turn a communist-era military base into a luxe resort
items.description: Ivanka Trump has floated "manifestations" of luxury holidays. Meanwhile, Albanians are claiming "irreversible" ecological damage. Why protests are shaking Albania.

items.title: SA Police investigating after man dies after 'ineffective' taser arrest
items.description: Police are investigating an incident at Clare, in South Australia's mid north, where a man became unresponsive during an arrest.

items.title: 'Beyond our capacity' to defend sea trade lanes, Shoebridge says
items.description: Greens defence spokesman David Shoebridge says it is "ridiculous" to think Australia's military could defend the nation's global trade lanes, and acquiring nuclear-powered submarines under AUKUS only invites Australia to a conflict between the United States and China.

items.title: How Tasmania's planned new stadium could trigger deal for Hobart Hurricanes
items.description: Cricket's smallest state says it could become a major player in privatisation, with a potential Hobart Hurricanes deal tied to Tasmania's planned Macquarie Point roofed stadium.

items.title: Missing Melbourne teacher allegedly murdered by brother in India
items.description: Indian authorities allege Melbourne maths teacher Sunil Sharma was murdered by his brother and dumped in a canal. He had been in India to prepare a property for sale.

items.title: Mourners farewell gangster a day after gunman targets wrong funeral venue
items.description: Dozens of mourners have turned out to farewell Sydney crime boss Lorenzo Lemalu at a funeral held at Lakemba Mosque, in Sydney's western suburbs.

items.title: I loved my body, even when it was expected I wouldn't get to love another
items.description: I'd take a cure for the pain, but I wouldn't take a cure for my appearance. This is who I am and why should I change myself to make other people more comfortable?

items.title: Meet the man born, raised and married in his local town hall
items.description: Brian Baker, 95, spent the first 21 years of his life in living quarters at the York Town Hall where his father was caretaker.

items.title: Planning, packing and nerves: Six Aussies kick off Race Around The World
items.description: Six Australian filmmakers are about to embark on the journey of a lifetime on Race Around The World. Here's how they're preparing for the unknown.

items.title: Debunking Australian weather's made-up terms and pseudoscience
items.description: Meteorological rhetoric in Australia, including from the media, can at times be inaccurate, misconstrued or just completely fictitious.

items.title: Commuters call for action after machete brawl at Flinders Street Station
items.description: Police say up to 10 people were fighting inside the station on Saturday night before some boarded a train still armed with machetes.

items.title: Homelessness service concerned by changing demographic in clients
items.description: As cost of living and housing pressures intensify, a South Australian homelessness service says more young women and single mothers are reaching out for support.

items.title: Private medical imaging provider bills Medicare for non-eligible services
items.description: A private medical imaging provider operating in a public hospital has been billing Medicare for some services that are not eligible for bulk billing, according to an internal memo obtained by the ABC.

items.title: Trump battles historians for ownership of US presidential records
items.description: The Trump administration is pushing for a return to pre-Nixon days when US presidents could do whatever they wanted with presidential records.

items.title: 'Cybertongue' could prevent 70 million tonnes of milk waste every year
items.description: About a sixth of the world's milk is wasted, over 150 million tonnes every year, but a Canberra company has come up with new technology that could drastically reduce that.

items.title: 'Right' decision: Lakemba Nights stallholders save thousands under changes
items.description: Considered as Australia's largest cultural festival, the Lakemba Nights food markets has been attracting more people every year amid the event's rising costs.

items.title: As vaccination rates fall in Australia, a British mother has a warning
items.description: Measles killed Rebecca Archer's daughter Renae slowly and silently over a decade. She has a message for the growing number of parents hesitant to have their children vaccinated.
